chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Mukhtār, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him عليه السلام: “Among us there is a man called Kulayb. Nothing comes from you except that he says: ‘I submit.’ So we named him Kulayb al-Taslīm.”
He said: So he invoked mercy upon him, then said: “Do you know what submission is?” So we remained silent. Then he said: “By Allah, it is al-ikhbāt.”
The saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: “Those who believe, and do righteous deeds, and humble themselves to their Lord.”

key_terms.أَخْبَتُوا: they humbled themselves; they became tranquil and submissive
key_terms.أُسَلِّمُ: I submit; an expression of accepting and yielding to the Imam’s teaching
key_terms.الْإِخْبَاتُ: humble inward submission and lowliness before Allah
key_terms.رَبِّهِمْ: their Lord; Allah as the One to whom humility and submission are directed
key_terms.عَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ: they did righteous deeds; performing acts of goodness and obedience

ai.seo_question: What does taslīm mean in the hadiths of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that true taslīm is not merely verbal agreement, but a state of humble surrender before Allah. The Imam عليه السلام interprets it through the Quranic description of those who believe, act righteously, and are inwardly humble toward their Lord.
